questions.prompt: What is the maximum applied pressure loss for a combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: With the service brake fully applied after stabilization, combination loss should not exceed 4 psi per minute.

questions.prompt: How is the low-air warning tested?
choices: Turn electrical power on and fan the brakes until the warning activates before pressure falls below the required level
Run the engine at high idle until the warning sounds
Set only the trailer hand valve
Drain one tank with the engine running at highway speed
questions.explanation: Fanning the service brake reduces stored pressure so the warning threshold can be observed.

questions.prompt: How is automatic spring-brake application checked?
choices: Continue fanning pressure down until the parking controls pop out in the manufacturer's range
Hold the accelerator down until the knobs pop out
questions.explanation: The test verifies that loss of air automatically triggers the emergency/parking brake controls.

questions.prompt: At 55 mph, about how much distance can air-brake lag add before braking begins?
questions.explanation: Air must travel through the system, adding roughly four-tenths of a second or about 32 feet at 55 mph.

questions.prompt: What pedal technique produces a smooth normal stop with air brakes?
choices: Apply controlled pressure, then release as needed to avoid a harsh stop
Hold the trailer hand valve down
questions.explanation: Controlled service-brake pressure manages deceleration without overheating or wheel lock.

questions.prompt: What is the service brake's role on a long, steep downgrade?
choices: Provide all speed control while the transmission is in neutral
questions.explanation: The correct gear and engine braking carry most of the load; properly timed service applications control speed.

questions.prompt: What operating error most directly causes brake fade on a downgrade?
choices: Continuous excessive brake use that overheats linings and drums
questions.explanation: Heat reduces friction and can expand drums away from the linings, weakening braking.

questions.prompt: How should a tractor-trailer with working ABS be braked in an emergency?
choices: Apply firm pressure and do not pump the pedal
Use the trailer hand valve only
Release the pedal when pulsation begins
Repeatedly set and release the parking brake
questions.explanation: ABS modulates wheel pressure automatically while the driver maintains firm braking.

questions.prompt: What should a driver do if the low-air warning comes on while moving?
choices: Stop safely before spring brakes apply automatically and have the system repaired
Pull the parking knob immediately in traffic
Continue until the next fuel stop
questions.explanation: Low pressure means available braking is being lost and automatic spring-brake application may follow.

questions.prompt: When may a driver leave an air-brake vehicle without setting the parking brakes?
choices: Only in a rare situation where very hot brakes or freezing conditions make spring-brake use unsafe, with wheels securely chocked
Whenever the stop will be under five minutes
questions.explanation: Parking brakes are normally mandatory; narrowly defined brake-temperature conditions require secure wheel chocks instead.

questions.prompt: Why should the brake pedal not be pushed when spring brakes are on?
choices: Combined spring and service force can damage brake components
It opens the safety valve at 60 psi
questions.explanation: Applying both forces together can overload brake hardware.

questions.prompt: In a dual system, what does one circuit at very low pressure mean?
choices: Either the front or rear service brakes may not operate fully, increasing stopping distance
The remaining circuit doubles its capacity
questions.explanation: A dual system may retain partial braking, but reduced capability requires an immediate safe stop.

questions.prompt: How often should manually drained air tanks be drained in normal service?
choices: At the end of each working day
Only when the low-air warning sounds
questions.explanation: Daily draining removes accumulated water and oil before they freeze or damage components.
questions.sourceReference: Section 5.4, Parking Brakes; Section 5.1, Air Tanks

questions.prompt: Why are combination vehicles more likely to roll over?
choices: They can have a high center of gravity and rearward amplification
Their trailers always have wider tires
Their engines are mounted too low
questions.explanation: Speed and steering movements can be amplified toward the rear of a combination.

questions.prompt: Which trailer in a multiple-trailer combination is most likely to roll over?
choices: Every trailer always rolls at the same time
questions.explanation: Rearward amplification makes the final trailer the most vulnerable to rollover.

questions.prompt: Why should steering inputs be smooth in a combination vehicle?
choices: Quick movements can cause trailer sway or rollover
questions.explanation: Smooth steering limits rearward amplification and helps keep the trailers stable.

questions.prompt: Why should a combination vehicle leave extra following distance?
choices: It needs more room to stop and avoid hard braking
The tractor is always shorter than a car
questions.explanation: Extra space reduces the need for abrupt braking that can cause skids or jackknifes.

questions.prompt: What can happen if trailer wheels lock during braking?
choices: The trailer may swing around in a jackknife
questions.explanation: Locked trailer wheels lose side grip and may slide sideways.

questions.prompt: What is offtracking?
choices: Rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels in a turn
A trailer moves faster than the tractor on a straight road
The fifth wheel slides by itself
questions.explanation: Offtracking requires the driver to allow enough room so trailer wheels clear curbs and objects.

questions.prompt: What is the safest basic backing setup for a trailer?
choices: Position so the trailer backs toward the driver's side when possible
Always back toward the blind side
Begin with the tractor sharply angled
questions.explanation: Driver-side backing provides better visibility and control.

questions.prompt: When backing a trailer, how should steering corrections be made?
choices: By using the trailer hand valve
questions.explanation: Small corrections prevent the trailer from rapidly moving out of line.

questions.prompt: What does trailer ABS help prevent?
questions.explanation: ABS helps maintain tire grip and stability during hard braking.

questions.prompt: Before coupling, how should trailer height compare with the fifth wheel?
choices: The trailer should be low enough to be raised slightly by the tractor
The trailer should be far above the fifth wheel
The kingpin should be below the pavement
questions.explanation: Proper height helps the kingpin enter the locking jaws and prevents a high hook.

questions.prompt: What is a high hook?
choices: The kingpin rides over or misses the fifth-wheel locking mechanism
The trailer air lines are crossed
The landing gear is fully raised
The tractor is in too low a gear
questions.explanation: A trailer set too high may let the fifth wheel pass under without securely capturing the kingpin.

questions.prompt: After the jaws lock, what should the driver do before raising the landing gear fully?
choices: Perform a gentle tug test against the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The tug test helps confirm that the fifth wheel has locked around the kingpin.

questions.prompt: What should be visible around a properly locked kingpin?
choices: The fifth-wheel jaws closed around the shank, not the head
A wide gap between the jaws
The release arm in the open position
The apron above the fifth wheel
questions.explanation: A visual inspection is essential even after a successful tug test.

questions.prompt: What should the fifth-wheel release arm show after coupling?
choices: It is in the locked position

questions.explanation: Passenger removal must not create a new safety hazard; the driver should follow company procedure and choose a safe place.

questions.prompt: Why must a passenger bus enter curves conservatively?
choices: Passengers have a higher center of gravity and may be standing or unbelted
questions.explanation: Smooth speed control protects vehicle stability and passengers who may not be restrained.

questions.prompt: Before pulling away from a stop, what sequence is safest?
choices: Close doors, account for passengers, check mirrors and traffic, then signal and move
Rely only on the left mirror
Move first and then check the curb
questions.explanation: A deliberate departure check prevents striking passengers, cyclists, or vehicles near the bus.

questions.prompt: Which action is prohibited while a passenger bus is moving?
choices: Fueling the bus with passengers aboard in a way forbidden by the manual or local rules
questions.explanation: Passenger-bus rules prohibit unsafe fueling, towing/pushing practices, and other operations that place riders at risk.

questions.prompt: Where should a passenger bus normally stop before railroad tracks?

With the front axle on the first rail
At least 100 feet away in every case
Only after the gate begins to lower
questions.explanation: The stop position provides sight distance without placing the bus in the track area.

questions.prompt: After stopping at a railroad crossing, what should the driver do before moving?

Follow the vehicle ahead without checking
Shift gears while on the tracks
Use the rear door interlock as the parking brake
questions.explanation: The driver must actively check for trains and avoid a missed shift on the tracks.

questions.prompt: When must a passenger bus stop before a drawbridge?
choices: When there is no traffic signal or attendant controlling the bridge
Every time, even when a green signal directs traffic
Only after entering the movable span
questions.explanation: Without active control, the driver must stop and verify the bridge is fully closed and safe.

questions.prompt: Why must a bus driver check space beyond the tracks before entering?
choices: The entire bus must clear the rails without stopping
Passengers may exit on the tracks
The gate will stay open longer
The transmission must be shifted on the crossing
questions.explanation: Long vehicles must never enter unless enough room exists on the far side.

questions.prompt: Which condition most strongly favors immediate bus evacuation?
choices: Fire, smoke, or a position where the bus may be struck
A passenger asking for fresh air
questions.explanation: Evacuate when remaining aboard presents greater danger than moving passengers to a safe area.

questions.prompt: After an evacuation begins, where should passengers be directed?
choices: To a safe assembly area away from traffic and the bus
questions.explanation: A controlled assembly point prevents secondary injuries and allows accountability.

questions.prompt: What must a driver generally complete before taking a passenger-bus skills test for the first time?
choices: Applicable passenger knowledge testing and required entry-level training
questions.explanation: The P endorsement has specific knowledge, training, and representative-vehicle testing requirements.

questions.prompt: Which endorsements are needed for a Nebraska school bus designed for 16 or more people including the driver?
questions.explanation: A qualifying school bus requires both P and S endorsements.
questions.sourceReference: Nebraska Specifics; Pupil Transportation Guide, Qualifications

questions.prompt: What is the danger zone around a school bus?
choices: The area around the bus where children are difficult for the driver to see
Any road more than a mile from school
questions.explanation: Children near the bus may be hidden in mirror blind spots, especially close to the front and sides.
questions.sourceReference: Section 10.1, Danger Zones and Use of Mirrors

questions.prompt: What should crossover mirrors show?
choices: The front bumper area and danger zones directly in front of the bus
Only traffic far behind the bus
The inside roof of the bus
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted crossover mirrors help reveal children near the front of the bus.

questions.prompt: When should school-bus mirror checks be made during loading?
choices: Continuously before, during, and after the stop
Once at the start of the route
questions.explanation: Children can move unpredictably, so mirror scanning must continue throughout the procedure.

questions.prompt: How should a school bus approach a student stop?

At normal road speed until the last moment
questions.explanation: A controlled approach gives students and motorists time to recognize the stop.

questions.prompt: Where should the bus stop for loading students?

With the front bumper touching the students' waiting area
Several feet from the curb with no reason
questions.explanation: Correct positioning minimizes exposure to traffic and keeps students visible.

questions.prompt: When students must cross the road, who should direct the crossing?
choices: The school-bus driver using the established signal and procedure
Students should cross whenever they choose
questions.explanation: The driver must account for traffic and signal when it is safe for students to cross.

questions.prompt: How far in front of the bus should students generally cross?
choices: Far enough to remain visible to the driver, commonly at least 10 feet
questions.explanation: Crossing well in front keeps students within the driver's field of view.

questions.prompt: What should a student do if an item is dropped near the bus?
choices: Tell the driver and wait for direction before retrieving it
Ask another student to crawl beneath the bus
Retrieve it after the bus begins moving
questions.explanation: The driver may not see a child bending near or under the bus.

questions.prompt: Why should the driver count students at a stop?
choices: To confirm everyone is safely aboard or clear before moving
questions.explanation: A count helps the driver account for children who might otherwise remain in a danger zone.

questions.prompt: Before moving after unloading, what should the driver do?

Close the door and move immediately
Sound the horn and skip mirror checks
Back up to view the curb
questions.explanation: The driver must be certain all students are safely away from the bus.

questions.prompt: When should backing a school bus be avoided?
choices: Whenever a safe alternative is available
questions.explanation: Backing creates blind-zone risk and should be minimized or performed with a spotter under controlled procedures.
questions.sourceReference: Section 10.2, Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading

questions.prompt: Where should a school bus stop at a railroad crossing?
choices: Between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail
With the front wheels on the rail
Only after the gate rises, without stopping
questions.explanation: School buses generally stop 15 to 50 feet away to look and listen for trains.

Proceed as soon as the first track is clear
Stop on the tracks to check the others
Follow the vehicle ahead without looking
questions.explanation: A train on one track may hide another train approaching on a different track.

questions.prompt: What gear should be used while crossing railroad tracks?
choices: A gear that allows crossing without shifting
The highest gear regardless of speed
questions.explanation: The driver should select an appropriate gear before entering and avoid shifting on the tracks.

questions.prompt: Which situation calls for immediate school-bus evacuation?

The interior lights fail in daylight

questions.prompt: Where should evacuated students be directed?
choices: To a safe location away from traffic and the bus
questions.explanation: The assembly point should protect students from traffic, fire, and other hazards.

questions.prompt: When should serious behavior problems be handled?

While looking away from the road
Only after opening the emergency exit
questions.explanation: The driver must maintain vehicle control and address behavior without becoming distracted.

questions.prompt: What is a critical post-trip school-bus check?
choices: Walk through and inspect for sleeping students, belongings, damage, or hazards
Lock the doors without entering the bus
Leave immediately after the last stop
questions.explanation: A complete post-trip inspection helps ensure no child remains aboard and identifies problems.
questions.sourceReference: Section 10.2; Pupil Transportation Guide, Post-trip Inspection

questions.prompt: How often must Nebraska pupils receive safe-riding instruction and participate in evacuation drills?
choices: At least twice each school year
questions.explanation: The Nebraska pupil transportation guide states that qualifying instruction and drills occur at least twice during each school year.

questions.prompt: Where is the most dangerous area around a school bus?
choices: Close to the bus where the driver may not see a child
questions.explanation: Children nearest the bus can disappear from direct and mirror view.

questions.prompt: When should the entrance door be opened at a student stop?
choices: After the bus is fully stopped and secured
Only after students touch the bus
questions.explanation: A secured stop prevents children from approaching a moving bus.

questions.prompt: What should students do before walking toward the bus?
choices: Wait for the driver's signal and for the bus to stop

questions.prompt: What should the driver check before signaling students across?

Move the bus into the motorist's lane
questions.explanation: Student movement must wait until the roadway is truly safe.

questions.prompt: Where should students move after leaving the bus?
choices: Directly to a safe location away from the danger zone
questions.explanation: Promptly clearing the bus area keeps children visible and safe.

questions.prompt: What should the driver do if a student cannot be accounted for after unloading?
choices: Keep the bus stopped and locate the student
Assume the child entered a building
questions.explanation: The bus must not move until every student is confirmed clear.

questions.prompt: If backing cannot be avoided, what support should be used when available?
choices: A student standing behind the bus
questions.explanation: A trained spotter helps monitor areas the driver cannot see.

questions.prompt: Why are route stops planned to minimize student crossings?
choices: Crossing traffic creates one of the greatest loading hazards
questions.explanation: Fewer road crossings reduce exposure to passing motorists.

questions.prompt: Which mirror system helps view the rear tires touching the ground?

questions.explanation: Side mirror coverage helps monitor rear wheel danger areas and traffic.

questions.prompt: What must the driver see in the student mirror?

questions.explanation: Interior mirror coverage supports student supervision and post-trip checks.

questions.prompt: What should the school-bus driver do with noise sources before listening for a train?
choices: Silence them and open the service door or window as required
questions.explanation: A quiet bus and an open listening point help detect an approaching train.

questions.prompt: Why must the driver check beyond the first set of tracks?
choices: A second train may be hidden by the first
The bus must change gears there
Warning lights cover only one rail
questions.explanation: Multiple tracks can carry trains from different directions.

questions.prompt: What should a driver do if a crossing signal activates while the bus is already crossing?
choices: Continue forward and clear the tracks without stopping
questions.explanation: Once committed, clearing the crossing is safer than stopping in the train path.

questions.prompt: Who should be assigned to help younger or mobility-limited students during a planned evacuation drill?
choices: Responsible helpers instructed by the driver
Students chosen after the emergency begins
questions.explanation: Preassigned helpers make evacuation faster and more orderly.

questions.prompt: What should be taken during an evacuation only if it is immediately available and safe?

questions.prompt: Where should disruptive students be seated when practical?
choices: Where the driver can monitor them without losing road attention
Beside an emergency exit they can block
questions.explanation: Seat placement may improve supervision while the driver remains focused on driving.

questions.prompt: Why should the driver check beneath seats during a post-trip inspection?
choices: A sleeping child or dangerous item may be hidden
questions.explanation: A deliberate walk-through must cover areas not visible from the aisle.

questions.prompt: When must Nebraska pupil-transportation headlights be used?
questions.explanation: The supplemental Nebraska guide requires headlights during operation.

questions.prompt: Outside a city or town, how closely may one Nebraska pupil-transportation vehicle follow another?

questions.explanation: The guide specifies a 475-foot convoy separation outside corporate limits.

questions.prompt: What should the driver do if students are standing too close as the bus approaches?
choices: Stop short and direct them to a safe waiting position
Continue to the normal stop point

questions.prompt: Why should students board one at a time using the handrail?

It allows the bus to keep moving

questions.prompt: What should a student do after reaching the road edge in front of the bus?

questions.prompt: Why must the driver watch for a late student approaching the stop?

Late students always approach from behind
The bus can move while the student boards
questions.explanation: Unexpected movement around the bus demands continued mirror and traffic checks.

choices: The child may enter a danger zone to retrieve it
questions.explanation: The driver must locate the child and control retrieval before moving.

questions.prompt: What should students be reminded to do after crossing in front of the bus?
choices: Continue to a safe location away from the roadway and bus

questions.prompt: When is the student count complete after unloading?
choices: When every student is located and safely clear of the bus
When the warning lights turn off
questions.explanation: The driver must account for each child before releasing brakes.

questions.prompt: Why should a school bus route be planned to avoid backing?
choices: Children and objects can disappear into large blind zones
Students are safer behind the bus
Backing reduces route time in every case
questions.explanation: Avoiding the maneuver removes a major danger-zone risk.

questions.prompt: If a spotter is lost from view while backing, what should the driver do?

questions.prompt: What should be visible in properly adjusted crossover mirrors?
choices: The front danger zone from the bumper outward

questions.prompt: Why should mirror adjustment be checked before the route begins?

questions.explanation: Correct coverage is essential before students enter danger zones.

questions.prompt: Why should the school bus stop with enough distance from the nearest rail?

To let students leave the bus
To shift gears on the rail
To block following traffic on the tracks
questions.explanation: The required stopping position provides a safe observation point.

questions.prompt: What should the driver verify on the far side before crossing?
choices: Enough room exists for the entire bus beyond the tracks

questions.prompt: Why should the bus cross railroad tracks in a gear that needs no shifting?
choices: A missed shift could stall the bus on the tracks
The train signal changes with engine speed
questions.explanation: Selecting the gear beforehand prevents loss of power while exposed.

questions.prompt: When may moving students off the bus create more danger than keeping them aboard?
choices: When traffic, weather, or outside hazards are worse than the condition inside
questions.explanation: The driver must compare immediate hazards before ordering an evacuation.

questions.prompt: Why should evacuation helpers know their assignments before an emergency?
choices: Prepared roles speed movement and student accountability
They may direct traffic from the roadway
They decide whether to call for help
questions.explanation: Practice reduces confusion and supports an orderly evacuation.

questions.prompt: What should the driver explain before the route about behavior expectations?
choices: Rules that keep aisles, exits, and driver attention clear
How to open exits while moving
Where to stand ahead of the line
questions.explanation: Clear expectations prevent conduct that interferes with safe operation.

questions.prompt: What should be checked after the last student leaves besides the seats?
choices: Floor, under seats, restrooms if equipped, and every rear area
questions.explanation: A deliberate sweep covers places where a child or dangerous item could remain hidden.

questions.prompt: Why must the bus capacity rating never be exceeded?
choices: Every student needs an intended seating position and vehicle limits must be respected
Capacity applies only off public roads
questions.explanation: Safe seating and rated weight limits protect occupants and vehicle control.

questions.prompt: What should a Nebraska pupil transportation driver do with a defect found during the pre-trip inspection?

questions.prompt: What area is included in a school bus danger zone?

Only the lane behind the bus
The area inside the passenger compartment

questions.prompt: When should alternating amber warning lights be activated for a school-bus stop?

With the rear of the bus blocking a railroad crossing

In the driver's mirror blind spot

The signal releases the parking brake
It turns off the red warning lights

The child should crawl under the bus quickly

Another child should retrieve it without signaling

questions.prompt: After unloading, what does counting students help the driver confirm?
choices: Every child is safely clear and no one remains in a danger zone
The mirrors no longer need to be checked

Ask students to guide the bus from behind

choices: A narrow part of the bus sides plus traffic lanes behind
The entire danger zone directly under the bus

choices: Show the danger areas directly in front of the bus and near the front wheels
Show only traffic a quarter mile behind
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors reveal children and objects hidden below the windshield near the front of the bus.

questions.prompt: Where must a school bus stop at a highway-rail crossing?

A student requesting a seat change
A failed radio with no other hazard
questions.explanation: The driver compares the danger of staying aboard with the danger of moving students.

Operate the bus on the highway
Stand in traffic to stop vehicles
Return to the bus for belongings

To count traffic behind the bus
